content.title: Tyson Fury dominates Arslanbek Makhmudov to set up potential Anthony Joshua mega-fight
content.text: Tyson Fury vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov headlined Saturday's Netflix fight card in London. (Richard Pelham via Getty Images)Tyson Fury and Conor Benn delivered underwhelming performances in their Netflix doubleheader.Fury won a near shutout (120-108, 119-109, 119-109) over Arslanbek Makhmudov — who had been previously stopped by Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello — in their heavyweight contest, and Benn defeated Regis Prograis by unanimous decision (98-92, 98-92, 98-92) in a 10-round, 150-pound catchweight bout Saturday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.AdvertisementAfter Fury beat Makhmudov, he made it clear he's setting his sights on a mega-fight with Anthony Joshua next."I want to give you the fight you've all been waiting for," Fury said to his fellow former world champion, who was sitting ringside. "I want you, AJ — Anthony Joshua. Let's give the fight fans what they want — the battle of Britain."And here's my challenge: I challenge you, Anthony Joshua, to fight me, 'The Gypsy King,' next. Do you accept my challenge?"Joshua refused to get in the ring to face off with Fury and also initially declined to respond to Fury's callout, instead choosing to stare his longtime rival down."Tyson, you're a clout chaser," Joshua responded eventually.Advertisement"I've never had no problem getting into the ring with you. I punched you up when we were kids, and after watching you here tonight, I'll punch you up again."With all due respect, tonight is your night, and you know I'll sit across that ring from you in due time," Joshua continued. "You ain't going to tell me what to do. I've been chasing you for the last 10 years. When you're ready, you come and see me and tell me your terms and conditions. And I'll have you in the ring when I'm ready."I'm the boss. You work for me. I'm the landlord. Remember that."Competing for the first time in 16 months, Fury (35-2-1, 24 KOs) comfortably outboxed Makhmudov (21-3, 19 KOs) over the distance. He controlled the action with his sharp jab and walked Makhmudov onto right uppercuts at close range. Fury also had plenty of success to the body. In the second half of the contest, Fury looked like he could force a stoppage on multiple occasions, but the Brit declined to go through the gears and force the finish — much to the disappointment of his corner. Makhmudov's tactics of wrestling and holding on the inside also aided his survival.AdvertisementOverall, it was a disappointing showing from Fury as two other heavyweight contenders were previously able to take Makhmudov out and looked more impressive in doing so than Fury did on Saturday. The performance also failed to excite the largely silent Tottenham crowd.In the co-feature, Benn's volume, body shots and jab proved to be too much for the faded Prograis (30-4, 24 KOs). Although Prograis found plenty of success with his southpaw left, he was outworked by Benn (25-1, 14 KOs) for large parts of the contest. Benn kept Prograis busy with an active jab and constantly threw his left hand at Prograis to score points and also to set up his power shots.Prograis was rocked by a right in the final few seconds of the opening round. His leg — which was rumored pre-fight to be injured — wobbled, and he looked off balance numerous times later in the contest. Benn suffered cuts to both eyes as a result of head clashes. Prograis had his best round in the fifth when a trio of lefts connected on the British contender, however Prograis began to offer less as the contest went on, and Benn labored to a decision win.AdvertisementFollowing Benn's victory, the former two-time 140-pound champion Prograis announced his retirement from boxing.Check out complete Fury vs. Makhmudov results and highlights below, as well as Uncrowned's play-by-play of the main card.Main cardHeavyweight: Tyson Fury def. Up close is safe if you're Tyson Fury.10-9 MakhmudovSat, April 11, 2026 at 4:04 PM CDTDarshan DesaiSat, April 11, 2026 at 4:02 PM CDTDarshan DesaiSat, April 11, 2026 at 4:00 PM CDTDarshan DesaiTyson Fury will end yet another retirement against Russia's Arslanbek Makhmudov in the main event.Fury has retired from boxing on at least five occasions, each one less convincing than the last. Thus, when Fury announced his comeback to the sport in January, hardly anyone was left surprised — except those who claim to know him the best, of course.Fury, 37, hasn't laced up his gloves for 16 months, not since a pair of 2024 defeats to Oleksandr Usyk, with the first of those two bouts being for the undisputed heavyweight championship.Makhmudov, 36, has landed this opportunity because of his decision win over the popular Dave Allen in Sheffield this past October. Prior to that, though, Makhmudov recorded stoppage losses against Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello, showing how he is far below world level.The Russian, 6-foot-7, matches Fury for height, but that is where the comparison stops. Makhmudov is stiff, defensively open and vulnerable — particularly to the body. Kabayel battered Makhmudov to the body while both Vianello and Allen had sizable success downstairs.Makhmudov, with 19 knockouts in 21 wins, is clearly heavy-handed, and Fury has been floored by lesser fighters, so Makhmudov certainly can have success if he lands big on Fury. Fury has also lost concentration in fights before and been caught with shots he shouldn't have been. But a puncher's chance may be where it ends for Makhmudov.Simply put, Fury is far too skilled for the Russian. And if he has anything left, this should look like the total mismatch it is. Fury's jab and movement are among the best in heavyweight boxing. He is a tactical master, boxing to game plans to defeat certain opponents. Fluent as both an orthodox and a southpaw, the Brit should have a full bag of tricks waiting for Makhmudov.The most interesting element in this fight is the question: How much does Fury have left? A veteran of 17 years in the paid ranks and the proud victor of a memorable but grueling trilogy with Deontay Wilder, it's fair to say that "The Gypsy King" has sustained a significant amount of wear and tear on his body.Pick: Fury
